For decades, ornithologists assumed that if they saw a singing Bell’s vireo—a bird species found
in temperate North America—they must be observing a male. That’s because birdsong has long
been considered a male trait; researchers have argued that singing enables males to attract mates
and claim territory.

of bias: much of the research ornithologists have carried out has been near universities in the
temperate northern hemisphere, where female birdsong is less common than it is in the tropics.

bioaccumulation in invertebrates like $L$. stagnalis could serve a valuable proxy role, obviating the

A run of river hydroelectric power plant, as the name suggests, uses the natural flow of a water
source to generate electricity but is unable to start or stop that flow through its generators. In
contrast, a peaking hydroelectric power plant (used when demand for electricity peaks) controls
